title: Route 53 + ACM + CloudFront
scenario: Serve a domain through CloudFront with a DNS-validated certificate and an alias record.
constraints: Create a hosted zone, ACM certificate and CloudFront distribution.
Create a Route 53 record in the zone.

focus.title: Complete the aws_cloudfront_distribution resource
focus.todo: Add the arguments and nested blocks required for aws_cloudfront_distribution.

hints.why: DNS is the public name of the system. Managing records in Terraform keeps the name, certificate and endpoint changes together.
hints.what: Complete the marked region in `main.tf`. The work is inside `resource "aws_cloudfront_distribution" "this"`. Add the arguments and nested blocks required for aws_cloudfront_distribution. Use the visible constraints as the checklist for names, values and references before you run the tests.
hints.when: Use Route 53 when a service needs a stable hostname or when DNS changes should be reviewed with the rest of the stack.
hints.how: Open `main.tf` and work only inside `resource "aws_cloudfront_distribution" "this"`. Use this code shape: enabled; default_cache_behavior { viewer_protocol_policy }; viewer_certificate { minimum_protocol_version; acm_certificate_arn; ssl_support_method }. Use the already-declared references instead of hardcoded values: `aws_acm_certificate.this.arn`. Keep the block header and braces, indent nested blocks by two spaces, and add one argument or nested block at a time. Run the tests after each small change so the first failure points at the next name to fix.
